cases.input: A desktop Electron app has 29 processes, 18 renderers, two independent account roots, two crash handlers, and no crash reports. Diagnose whether this proves zombies or a crash loop.
A health script reports HTTP FAIL but the script probes a Microsoft connectivity URL while the incident concerns OpenAI. Direct service-specific requests return low-latency HTTP responses.
Windows UI Automation bounding rectangles are compared with coordinates from a DPI-virtualized client at 200 percent scaling, and a guard declares the composer missing.
A polling guard can inject Ctrl+R when a control is judged missing during layout transitions. The UI symptom existed before the guard, but reload capability could amplify churn or input loss.
A skill and configuration exist in GitHub, but no owning runtime has loaded or executed them.
Two desktop accounts run simultaneously with similar process names but different roots, profiles, logs, and automation sessions.
A model usage cap is enforced by a cloud provider while the local machine has recently received more RAM.
A local bridge recovers after being unavailable, but previous session IDs and target affinity may be stale.
A CI job fails before any project test step because the runner or artifact fetch is unavailable.
Two CLI entrypoints resolve to different versions, and an npx latest path changes over time.
Desktop text automation intermittently fails because another application steals foreground/input ownership during the write.
An agent returns a correct final answer after duplicate tool side effects, a stale handoff, and an unnecessary retry storm.
